transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-12-22 14:30 PT | Duration: ~48m | Platform: Zoom (recording)
Attendees (recorded): Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Luis Ortega (Redwood SE); Avery Chen (Redwood CSM); Sofia Reyes (CopperTrail Head of ML); Marcus Lin (PM); Anika Patel (Data Privacy); Devon Cho (ML Eng); Raj Shah (Ops)
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): okay hey everyone thanks for carving out time this afternoon, quick agenda: heatmap recap, prompt surgery, guardrail options, security/pricing check, and then action items. sound good?
[00:14] Sofia (CopperTrail): yep that works, we mostly want to see the failing buckets again — the returns flow and a few hallucination spots.
[00:23] Luis (Redwood): great, i'll share my screen with the eval dashboard — apologies if the headings are a bit off, the CSV had some utf8 funnyness so some names got mangled.
[00:35] [screen share noise] Luis (Redwood): ok so top left is overall pass/fail rate across the 12k test prompts, last run after your prompt updates was 86% pass by our default threshold. but if you look at the heatmap, you can see two dense clusters: "policy-violation-ish" false positives around returns language, and hallucination tail cases for sku lookup where the model invents vendor names.
[01:05] Marcus (CopperTrail): when you say 86% is that at the score >= .7 threshold? we used .75 locally so that explains some mismatch.
[01:12] Luis (Redwood): yeah this is our baseline .7 — we can shift to .75 and rerun but that typically trades recall for precision. we flagged three of the failure buckets: canonicalization issues, truncation/prefix tokenization, and guardrail false positives.
[01:30] Devon (CopperTrail): the truncation ones are mostly longer customer messages where they paste order threads. is there a way to preserve the tail context without blowing token cost?
[01:40] Luis (Redwood): two levers — prefix KV-cache helps if the same customer id or order id patterns repeat, and also you can run our async retriever short-circuit (i.e., fetch structured order metadata first, pass only minimal context). both will reduce repeated tokens and keep latency stable. caching is dependent on session semantics though, so cache keys need careful design.
[02:04] Anika (CopperTrail): on caching — we need to confirm KMS behavior, encrypted cache at rest etc. we can't have plaintext customer PII in long-term cache.
[02:15] Avery (Redwood): for sure, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we have encrypted-at-rest with per-tenant keys and audit logs. we will attach the SOC2 summary and KMS integration doc after the call.
[02:30] Sofia (CopperTrail): okay good. back to prompts — the returns language: sometimes the team writes "refund because wrong item" and other times "return due to fit" — that variability causes the classifier to oscillate.
[02:42] Luis (Redwood): that sounds like label distribution shift. i recommend prompt canonicalization — a tiny preprocessor that maps common phrases to canonical slots, e.g., map "wrong item" -> [reason_wrong_item]. we can add that as a syntactic guardrail upstream so the model sees normalized forms.
[02:58] Marcus (CopperTrail): can Redwood run the canonicalizer as part of the pipeline or do we need to own it?
[03:05] Maya (Redwood): we can implement it as a lightweight pre-route transform in the hosted pipeline as part of the pilot. for Private/Dedicated customers you can run it in your sidecar if you want full control. there's a tradeoff in operational ownership.
[03:20] [00:03:30] Luis (Redwood): diving into the hallucination cases — we found a recurrence pattern: prompts that include partial sku numbers plus casual vendor mentions cause the model to invent plausible-sounding vendors. our scoring flagged them in the 0.3-0.5 band.
[03:42] Devon (CopperTrail): can we set a threshold and then do a fallback to a structured lookup when score < 0.6?
[03:48] Luis (Redwood): yes, two-tier policy recommended: if answer_confidence < threshold, then call the structured lookup or return a clarifying question. we can model-call fallback with no extra infra, Redwood routes the flow — but for consistent latency you might want an in-process retriever.
[04:05] Raj (CopperTrail): latency, yes — what was the 95th percentile on your benchmark for these flows? we're trying to keep under 600ms for UI responses.
[04:12] Luis (Redwood): current hosted POC run with batching disabled for UI paths is hitting ~420ms p95 on the short prompts, but the long-order-threads push p95 to ~1.2s. batching can help throughput but increases tail latency, so we suggested dynamic batching where UI routes bypass batching and background processes use larger batches.
[04:34] Marcus (CopperTrail): is that an option on Dedicated? we might need burst lanes for UI spikes.
[04:40] Maya (Redwood): Dedicated supports burst lanes and configurable autoscaling policies; we also have a Dedicated+burst offering for predictable p95 with an SLA. i'll include pricing options in the follow-up.
[04:55] [00:05:00] Sofia (CopperTrail): quick Q on scoring: you mentioned moving the score threshold — are you doing calibrated probabilities or raw logit conversion?
[05:03] Luis (Redwood): we calibrate with Platt scaling over your validation fold — so the score is calibrated-ish but dependent on prompt distribution. when you shift the threshold you change the operating point; we prefer to show PR curves for intended tradeoff.
[05:18] Devon (CopperTrail): can you attach the per-prompt scores and the exact prompt text so we can reproduce?
[05:23] Luis (Redwood): yes — nightly batch will dump prompt text, score, and failure bucket. note: we sometimes redact PII automatically and that can change tokenization; we'll flag redacted rows.
[05:36] Anika (CopperTrail): that's important — any exported CSVs must be compatible with our governance rules. we will need an S3 location with VPC endpoints and SSE-KMS.
[05:48] Luis (Redwood): understood, we can push results to your S3 with customer-managed KMS on Private/Dedicated or to a temporary secure link for hosted.
[06:00] Maya (Redwood): switching gears — guardrail approaches: we propose a layered model: 1) syntactic filters (regexes, canonicalizer), 2) calibrated score thresholds + fallback, 3) model variant rollbacks (move to safer, smaller model under high-risk conditions).
[06:18] Marcus (CopperTrail): model variant rollbacks — are those instantaneous? we have compliance windows where we must ensure responses never exceed certain risk.
[06:25] Luis (Redwood): yes rollbacks can be configured as traffic policy rules — instantaneous routing to safety model if a route metric crosses a threshold; there's a brief warmup for a cold model but fallback works instantly for new requests. you can also pin users to specific model variants.
[06:40] Sofia (CopperTrail): warmup times are a concern; if the safety model is cold it could increase latency. any mitigation?
[06:45] Luis (Redwood): pre-warm pools or keep a minimal hot replica for the safety model. Dedicated makes that easy because you can reserve capacity for safety lanes.
[06:55] [00:07:10] Marcus (CopperTrail): okay, let's talk numbers — after canonicalization and threshold tweak you think we can get to >92% pass on returns and reduce hallucinations by 60%?
[07:03] Luis (Redwood): based on the simulated run we saw a projected pass of 91-94% depending on your threshold and whether you accept the precision recall tradeoff. hallucinations dropped ~58% when we turned on the retriever fallback in the simulation.
[07:18] Sofia (CopperTrail): good — one more org question: legal wants the audit log granularity for SSO events and per-request decision traces for safety reviews. can we do that?
[07:28] Avery (Redwood): yes, Redwood Console has per-request traces with token-level cost and decision metadata. for Private/Dedicated you can push logs to your SIEM; hosted gives long-form audit logs with redaction options.
[07:45] Anika (CopperTrail): and the per-request traces, do they contain the full prompt? our policy says we can't persist full PII prompts in logs.
[07:53] Luis (Redwood): we support redaction hooks in the ingestion pipeline — we can strip or hash identified PII before retention. that is configurable per route.
[08:05] Raj (CopperTrail): deployment timeline — if we want Dedicated with burst for January pilot extension, is that realistic?
[08:12] Maya (Redwood): operationally yes but lead time depends on contract and infra region. provisioning Dedicated nodes takes 7–14 days after contract signature for common regions. for immediate needs we can enable Hosted burst lanes while Dedicated is provisioned.
[08:26] Marcus (CopperTrail): can you remind us of the pricing delta for burst capacity versus baseline?
[08:30] Maya (Redwood): i'll include the tiered pricing in the follow-up; rough ballpark is 2.2–2.8x per-token for low-latency burst lanes depending on committed volume.
[08:40] [00:09:10] Sofia (CopperTrail): let's align on the pilot extension criteria. our internal success metric is 95% pass on the returns set and p95 < 600ms for UI routes.
[08:50] Luis (Redwood): sounds clear. i suggest a two-week validation window after you accept the prompt canonicalizer and threshold settings. we run the nightly sweep and provide the per-prompt CSV so you can validate offline.
[09:05] Devon (CopperTrail): for the nightly sweep, how many examples will you run? our test suite is currently 12k but we might add another 4k edge cases.
[09:12] Luis (Redwood): no problem — we can scale to 25k in the nightly job; only caveat is longer runtime but results will be available by morning.
[09:20] Anika (CopperTrail): legal wants timeboxed retention for the nightly outputs; can you set retention to 7 days by default?
[09:26] Avery (Redwood): yes retention is configurable per objective; we can set 7 days for the pilot exports and longer for audit logs if needed.
[09:35] [00:10:00] Maya (Redwood): quick recap — Luis will run the expanded nightly eval with edge cases and push CSV to CopperTrail S3 (with KMS). Sofia to share the two edge-case prompt groups. Maya to send pricing and SOC2/KMS docs. Anika to confirm legal timeline.
[09:50] Marcus (CopperTrail): any other blockers?
[09:55] Sofia (CopperTrail): just one more: can we get a short runbook for when a model rollback happens? our ops folks want steps and who-owns-what.
[10:03] Luis (Redwood): yes i can draft a 1-pager: alert triggers, rollback steps, verification checks, and re-promote steps. will include sample metrics to watch.
[10:15] Maya (Redwood): perfect. i'll put tentative follow-up on Wednesday for a short demo of the canonicalizer and to confirm the CSV transfer.
[10:25] [00:10:40] Sofia (CopperTrail): thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[10:29] [meeting end with small chatter]
Notes on transcription: small speaker mislabels and occasional words fused together are present due to transcription engine; names like "KV cache" sometimes rendered as "K V cache" and Redwood product names may be slightly off.
